summary: This Wikipedia-derived note surveys the Ottoman Empire, covering its demographics, naval and military history, cuisine, architecture, language, governance, and eventual dissolution. It traces the empire's founding by Osman I around 1299, its expansion under Suleiman the Magnificent, its decline and the Treaty of Sèvres, and the abolition of the sultanate in 1922 and caliphate in 1924. It also describes migrations, the carpet-weaving tradition, and the economic role of Christian and Jewish communities.
one_line: Overview of the Ottoman Empire's history, governance, military, culture, demographics and dissolution from 1299 to 1924.
key_facts: The Ottoman Empire was founded in 1299 by Oghuz Turks under Osman I in northwestern Anatolia.
The Ottomans ended the Byzantine Empire with the 1453 conquest of Constantinople by Mehmed the Conqueror.
The Muslim proportion of the empire's population was 60% in the 1820s, rising to 69% in the 1870s and 76% in the 1890s.
By 1914, only 19.1% of the empire's population was non-Muslim, mostly Christian Greeks, Assyrians, Armenians, and Jews.
The Portuguese discovery of the Cape of Good Hope in 1488 initiated a series of Ottoman-Portuguese naval wars in the Indian Ocean throughout the 16th century.
In the Battle of Ankara in 1402, Timur defeated the Ottoman forces and took Sultan Bayezid I as a prisoner.
Suleiman the Magnificent captured Belgrade in 1521 and won the Battle of Mohács in 1526.
The Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca of 1774 ended the Russo-Turkish War of 1768–1774 and provided freedom to worship for Christian citizens of Wallachia and Moldavia.
The Armistice of Mudros was signed on 30 October 1918, setting the partition of the Ottoman Empire under the Treaty of Sèvres.
The sultanate was abolished on 1 November 1922, and the last sultan, Mehmed VI, left the country on 17 November 1922.
The caliphate was abolished on 3 March 1924.
In 1911, of the 654 wholesale companies in Istanbul, 528 were owned by ethnic Greeks.
The Ottoman Navy Foundation was established in 1910 to buy new ships through public donations.
The Turkish War of Independence (1919–22) was won under the leadership of Mustafa Kemal, later given the surname Atatürk.
Ottoman Turkish was an Oghuz Turkic language highly influenced by Persian and Arabic and was the official language of the Empire.

entities.role: empire founded in 1299 by Oghuz Turks under Osman I, later a transcontinental empire and claimant to the caliphate

entities.role: founder of the Ottoman Empire and of the ruling House of Osman

entities.name: Bayezid I

entities.name: Mehmed VI

entities.name: Mustafa Kemal

entities.name: Abdülhamid II

entities.name: Midhat Pasha
entities.role: reformist whose admirals sided with him, distrusted by Sultan Abdülhamid II

entities.name: Abdülaziz

entities.name: Vasco da Gama

entities.name: Christopher Columbus

entities.name: Marco Polo

entities.name: Justin McCarthy
